# Iraq suffer Ahmed Yahya injury blow ahead of FIFA World Cup 2026
[...]
Iraq lost defender Ahmed Yahya to injury, prompting a late squad change before the World Cup.
[...]
Iraq’s preparations for the 2026 FIFA World Cup have been disrupted by a significant injury setback, with defender Ahmed Yahya ruled out of the tournament due to a hamstring problem. The late withdrawal has forced the coaching staff to make a change to the squad just days before the team’s campaign begins.
[...]
Ahmed Yahya was expected to be an important part of Iraq’s defensive setup at the World Cup. However, medical examinations confirmed that the defender would not recover in time to participate in the tournament.
[...]
The injury comes as a blow to Iraq, which is preparing for its first World Cup appearance in four decades. Yahya played a key role during the qualification campaign and brought valuable experience to the squad. His absence leaves a gap in the backline, forcing head coach Graham Arnold to rethink his defensive options ahead of the opening match.
[...]
🚨 Squad UpdateMedical tests have confirmed that Ahmed Yahya has sustained an injury in the Spain match.Graham Arnold has called up Ahmed Mkenzi to replace Ahmed Yahya in the final squad for the 2026 World Cup finals.Wishing Ahmed Yahya a speedy recovery. 🇮🇶⚽ pic.twitter.com/aSccfIGjrU
[...]
To address the setback, Iraq has called up Ahmed Hassan Makenzie as Yahya’s replacement. The defender joined the squad in Chicago, where the team is finalising preparations before the tournament gets underway.
[...]
The Iraqi squad remains focused despite the disruption. Arnold and his coaching staff have continued preparations with the aim of ensuring the team is ready for the challenge ahead. Iraq enters the competition with confidence after a successful qualification campaign and hopes to compete strongly against some of the world’s best teams.
[...]
Drawn alongside France, Senegal and Norway, Iraq faces a difficult task in the group stage. Experienced players such as Aymen Hussein and Zidane Iqbal are expected to play key roles as the team looks to overcome the loss of Yahya and make a positive impression on its long-awaited return to the World Cup stage.

results.title: A painful blow for Iraq before the World Cup... and an emergency replacement called up - Roya News
highlights:
A painful blow for Iraq before the World Cup... and an emergency replacement called up - Roya News

#### On Friday evening, the Iraqi national football team delegation headed to America to participate in the 2026 World Cup, after concluding its preparation program which included an intensive training camp and friendly matches that resulted in positive results that enhanced the readiness of the “Lions of Mesopotamia” before the start of the global tournament.

The Iraqi national team had concluded its preparations with an exciting 1-1 draw against European champions Spain in a friendly match held last Thursday evening, following a 1-0 victory over Andorra in a previous test, which gave the coaching staff great confidence in the team’s ability to compete strongly during the global football tournament.

But Australian coach Graham Arnold, the technical director of the Iraqi national team, received a painful blow during the match against “La Roja”, after left-back Ahmed Yahya suffered a muscle injury that forced him to leave the field before the end of the match, which prompted Arnold to make an immediate decision to call up player Ahmed Maknazi to join the national team’s delegation as an emergency replacement.

The move to call up McKenzie came as a precautionary measure by the former coach of the Australian national team, in anticipation of the possibility that Ahmed Yahya’s injury might worsen and prevent him from participating in international competitions, especially since the initial medical examinations have not yet determined the extent of the injury suffered by the Police Club player.

Ahmed Yahya is scheduled to undergo comprehensive medical examinations as soon as the Iraqi delegation arrives in the United States, where the team's medical staff will determine his physical readiness and the possibility of his participation in the World Cup finals, or the need to rely on the substitute, McKenzie, throughout the tournament.

results.title: World Cup 2026: Iraq squad includes Ali Al-Hamadi and Zidane Iqbal - BBC Sport
highlights:
World Cup 2026: Iraq squad includes Ali Al-Hamadi and Zidane Iqbal - BBC Sport

Getty Images

Ali Al-Hamadi and Zidane Iqbal were part of Iraq's squad for their World Cup play-off win over Bolivia in Mexico

Ben Collins

BBC Sport journalist

1 June 2026

Ipswich forward Ali Al-Hamadi and Manchester United youth product Zidane Iqbal are part of Iraq's squad for the 2026 World Cup.

But coach Graham Arnold left out Dundee United defender Dario Naamo, who recently switched his international allegiance from Finland and made his Iraq debut in Friday's 1-0 friendly win over Andorra.

Ahmed Qasem also made his debut on Friday, after switching from Sweden, and the Nashville SC midfielder is included Arnold's 26-man squad.

Al-Hamadi's family fled Iraq when he was a baby and settled in Liverpool, where he was signed by Tranmere before making his EFL debut with Wycombe in 2022.

The 24-year-old became the first Iraqi player to feature in the Premier League with Ipswich in 2024 and spent the season just completed on loan with Luton in League One.

Al-Hamadi and experienced forward Aymen Hussein scored as Iraq beat Bolivia 2-1 in the World Cup play-offs to qualify for the first time in 40 years, while Iqbal was an unused substitute.

The Manchester-born midfielder, 23, came through United's academy and made one Champions League appearance before joining Dutch side Utrecht in 2023, playing 18 times last season.

Goalkeeper Jalal Hassan is Iraq's captain and their most experienced player with 100 caps. Australian coach Arnold has kept fellow keeper Kamil Saadi with the squad, in addition to the three goalkeepers he has selected, in case of an injury.

Iraq have been drawn in Group I and will face Norway in Boston, France in Philadelphia and then Senegal in Toronto.

## Iraq's World Cup squad

Goalkeepers: Fahad Talib (Al-Talaba), Jalal Hassan (Al-Zawraa), Ahmed Basil (Al-Shorta).

Defenders: Hussein Ali (Pogon Szczecin), Manaf Younis, Ahmed Yahya, Mustafa Saadoon (Al-Shorta), Zaid Tahseen (Pakhtakor), Rebin Sulaka (Port), Akam Hashim (Al-Zawraa), Merchas Doski (Viktoria Plzen), Zaid Ismail (Al-Talaba), Frans Putros (Persib).

Midfielders: Amir Al-Ammari (Cracovia), Kevin Yakob (Aarhus GF), Zidane Iqbal (Utrecht), Aimar Sher (Sarpsborg), Ibrahim Bayesh (Al-Dhafra), Ahmed Qasem (Nashville SC), Youssef Amyn (AEK Larnaca), Marko Farji (Venezia).

Forwards: Ali Jassim (Al-Najma), Ali Al-Hamadi (Ipswich), Ali Yousef (Al-Talaba), Aymen Hussein (Al-Karma), Mohanad Ali (Dibba).

results.title: Coach Arnold satisfied with Iraq's performance despite 2-0 Venezuela loss - Iraqi News
highlights:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi national football team concluded its World Cup preparatory matches with a 2-0 defeat against Venezuela in Chicago on Wednesday, June 10, 2026. Despite the scoreline, head coach Graham Arnold expressed his overall satisfaction with the squad’s tactical discipline and organization, framing the high-intensity fixture as a vital final learning step before the 2026 FIFA World Cup officially gets underway.
[...]
Speaking to the press after the final whistle, in comments monitored by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Arnold highlighted the physical demands his players have faced over the past week:
[...]
“It was a solid match from an organizational and disciplinary standpoint. Coming off a highly demanding clash against Spain in Europe, it was clear that the team was still processing the heavy physical rhythm and quick turnaround of that intense encounter.”
[...]
The Australian strategist noted that the game turned on minor defensive lapses, which his coaching staff intends to rectify immediately before entering group play:
[...]
“The team committed only two isolated defensive errors during the entire ninety minutes. We will treat these mistakes as valuable teaching moments and crucial opportunities for tactical refinement ahead of our official matches.”
[...]
Arnold emphasized that the overall performance remained positive, highlighting that the single most important victory of the night was the physical preservation of his roster:
[...]
“The most critical takeaway from this match is that we managed to exit a highly physical game with zero injuries across the entire squad. Maintaining optimal player health and physical readiness is our absolute, baseline priority as we stand on the cusp of the World Cup.”
